title: VP: The majority won’t support me if I’m wrong
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has maintained her innocence, saying she still enjoys the support of the majority of the people despite all the accusations hurled against her before the Senate…

blocks.text: November 26, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte led the commemoration of the 128th Araw ng Kalayaan at Rizal Park in Davao City on June 12, 2026.
Facebook / Inday Sara Duterte

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has maintained her innocence, saying she still enjoys the support of the majority of the people despite all the accusations hurled against her before the Senate impeachment court.
In an interview with Politiko, Duterte said she continues to draw strength from her followers amid speculative reports that the senator-judges have made up their minds ahead of the final verdict.
“I think that God would not have put me here if He didn’t have a purpose, right? God is not that unreasonable. I trust His purpose. I have faith. He is there somewhere watching,” Duterte said.
Reports said senators have secured the numbers to convict the Vice President, currently facing serious allegations of unexplained wealth.
“Even with so many attacks, so much mudslinging, the people are still there, especially in 2016, 2019, 2022. Last year, they helped. They didn’t leave, they didn’t give up,” Duterte added.

Certain legal quarters have said Duterte could resign before a guilty verdict is reached to spare her from the penalty of disqualification from public office. Resignation will then allow her to pursue her presidential bid in 2028. “It gives me confidence that I am right because how can the majority be there for me if I am wrong? That means the majority is wrong. So that gives me confidence that I am right, because the people are there,” Duterte noted.
Other legal experts, however, said disqualification from public office automatically goes hand-in-hand with conviction.
The impeachment court will resume trial sessions on Dec. 1, as the tribunal targets a final judgment before Congress adjourns on Dec. 18.
Defense spokesman Michael Poa said the legal team of Duterte is expected to present at least five to six witnesses in the coming weeks.
Thanksgiving
The Vice President and her allies, including former president and Pampanga Rep. Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, gathered over the weekend for a thanksgiving party.

During the Kapihan sa Manila Bay forum, Bagong Henerasyon (BH) party-list Rep. Robert Nazal and his wife, former representative Bernadette Herrera, confirmed that the occasion was held in their house.

“Basically, she probably just wanted to thank her supporters, especially those (congressmen) who voted no to the impeachment. She conducts thanksgiving every year, when Christmas is approaching. It was like an early celebration of the Christmas season for those who helped her,” Nazal said.
For her part, Herrera said some of the allies of Duterte were not able to attend the get-together as they were abroad.

“Because it was a last-minute thing, many were out of the country because every year, she organizes a get-together so she just wanted to gather politicians first because every year, she really invites different sectors,” Herrera noted.
According to Herrera, the ongoing impeachment trial was not discussed.
“She told us, she just wanted to get together, no politics. She didn’t want to talk about politics. She just wanted to say thank you,” Herrera said.
She added that Duterte also held a thanksgiving party for bloggers who support her.
“The bloggers were invited to the Vice President’s office,” she said.
Herrera said Duterte does not want to discuss politics until the impeachment trial is over.
